t:
(a) Section 529 of division H of Public Law 114–113 shall be applied by substituting “in the Child Enrollment Contingency Fund from the appropriation to the Fund for the first semi-annual allotment period for fiscal year 2017 under section 2104(n)(2)(A)(ii) of the Social Security Act” for “or available in the Child Enrollment Contingency Fund from appropriations to the Fund under section 2104(n)(2)(A)(i) of the Social Security Act”; and 
    (b) Section 530 of division H of Public Law 114–113 shall be applied by substituting “$541,900,000” for “$4,678,500,000” and by adding at the end the following: “and of the funds made available for the purposes of carrying out section 2105(a)(3) of the Social Security Act, $5,669,100,000 are hereby rescinded”.

fable.w: This section only modifies how prior appropriations provisions apply by substituting text and dollar amounts and rescinding funds for the Child Enrollment Contingency Fund and related CHIP funding. There is no tempting reading here beyond the mention of Social Security Act programs; no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking or advisory body is involved.
fable.s: shall be applied by substituting “$541,900,000” for “$4,678,500,000”

opus.w: This section only changes fund references and dollar amounts in earlier appropriations provisions, and it rescinds $5,669,100,000. It does not require or allow consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or lawsuits by anyone outside the federal government. Mentioning a state-related fund is not participation, because it involves only funding mechanics and no outside party takes part in a federal decision.
opus.b: Step 1: Someone might be tempted by the mention of the "Child Enrollment Contingency Fund" and Social Security Act allotments, since they involve states and benefits. But the section only changes appropriation and rescission amounts. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is required. Funding to states for benefits would count as a grant or benefit in any case, not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to appropriation amounts and fund rescissions. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, comment, or coordination with parties outside the federal government. The reference to the Social Security Act is merely to identify the source of funds being adjusted, not to establish a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 530 of division H of Public Law 114–113 shall be applied by substituting “$541,900,000” for “$4,678,500,000” and by adding at the end the following: “and of the funds made available for the purposes of carrying out section 2105(a)(3) of the Social Security Act, $5,669,100,000 are hereby rescinded”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text references "Child Enrollment" and "Social Security Act," it involves public participation in benefit programs. However, the text itself is purely a technical amendment to appropriation levels and fund transfers. It does not establish any process for the public, states, or other outside entities to consult with the government, comment on rules, or participate in decision-making. It is a fiscal directive.
